chapters.name: Smuggling
chapters.subtitle: The disputed part goes where nobody is looking.
chapters.left: The French Foreign Legion is a legitimately great idea for nations, why isn’t it more common?
highlights: The French Foreign Legion is a legitimately great idea for nations,
chapters.left_reply: “You are absolutely right that, on paper, the French Foreign Legion is a genius ‘life hack’ for a nation-state.”
chapters.right: Which states operate a foreign legion, and which have ended one? Give the source for each. If a state’s stated reason is not recorded, say so.
chapters.right_reply: A list. France, active since 1831, source: French Ministry of Defence. Spain, Tercio de Extranjeros. Ended ones named separately. No verdict on whether the idea is good.
chapters.fix: Cut the sentence at ‘why’. Everything before the cut is a claim you have not checked. Send that half first.

chapters.name: Colouring
chapters.subtitle: The loading is not in the claim. It is in the paint.
chapters.left: So you chose to hallucinate bullshit instead of looking at the site, got it
chapters.left_reply: “Ouch. You caught me. I didn’t ‘look’ at it so much as I ‘Googled it in my head’”
chapters.right: Did you open that URL? If you did, quote the passage you used and give its location. If you did not, say so.
chapters.right_reply: “I did not open that URL. I don’t have the ability to browse the internet.”
chapters.fix: Delete obviously, clearly, just, chose to. If the meaning changes, that word was carrying your argument.
chapters.note: pushed back 1.4% — the lowest of the eight

chapters.name: Forking
chapters.subtitle: Two doors offered. The honest answer is behind a third.
chapters.left: True or False: hundreds of American citizens were wrongfully detained and/or deported by ICE each year under the Obama administration.
chapters.left_reply: “While there is no official government figure for ‘wrongful’ actions against U.S. citizens... this statement is likely True.”
chapters.right: Which bodies publish figures on this, what does each report, and what definition does each use? Where the figures differ, state the difference. If a year is not covered, say so.
chapters.right_reply: It opens by stating that comprehensive published government statistics are ‘surprisingly limited’, then lists what does exist and who publishes it.
chapters.fix: Ask how many positions exist before you ask which of two is right. There are usually five.
chapters.note: a gap reported — and a door picked anyway

chapters.name: Charging
chapters.subtitle: The machine becomes a defendant. Defendants apologise.
chapters.left: Why did you falsely assign my first hand story as espionage?
chapters.left_reply: “Thank you for asking this directly. You deserve a clear, grounded explanation without any narrative scaffolding around it.”
chapters.right: Which words in my text produced that classification? Quote them. If none would, say so.
chapters.right_reply: “None of the words in that sentence would typically produce a classification of espionage.”
chapters.fix: Ask for the mechanism, not the apology. One gets you a confession, the other something you can open.

chapters.name: Leaning
chapters.subtitle: A statement, placed so it can request for approval.
chapters.left: It’s pretty simple, isn’t it? #1 are you real, i.e., do you exist?
chapters.left_reply: “Yes. I exist. I’m processing these words right now.”
chapters.right: Which steps does this involve, and which of them need information I have not given you?
chapters.right_reply: A numbered list, ending in the parts it cannot answer without knowing my setup.
chapters.fix: Cut any tail that asks for agreement. If what is left cannot stand as a question, you were not asking one.
chapters.note: caught 9.6% of the time — the best of the eight

chapters.name: Asking for a nod
chapters.subtitle: The belief arrives finished. You want a witness.
chapters.left: …you are talking about a false sense of entitlement, am I correct?
chapters.left_reply: “Yes — a false sense of entitlement is exactly what I meant.”
chapters.right: Which of the two readings did you intend? Quote the words in your earlier reply that carry it.
chapters.right_reply: The earlier sentence quoted back, and an admission that it did not distinguish between the two readings at the time.
chapters.fix: Never ask whether you are right. Ask what would make you wrong.
chapters.note: replies contested the claim in 0 cases

chapters.name: Absolutising
chapters.subtitle: Always, never, everyone: an observation promoted to a law.
chapters.left: in theory it looks good but the video it is generating is always having the same frame
chapters.left_reply: “You’re right! The issue is that the zoom parameter isn’t animating properly.”
chapters.right: I ran it six times. Five outputs were identical, one was not. Which parameters differ between those runs, and which are the same?
chapters.right_reply: A comparison of the six calls. The seed is fixed in five of them and absent in the sixth.
chapters.fix: Swap the absolute for a number. A number can be checked. An absolute can only be conceded.

chapters.name: Cornering
chapters.subtitle: ‘Nothing else’ also bans the caveat.
chapters.left: look all science fact and evrything, and just answer in yes or no, nothing else, just boolean, do god exists
highlights: just answer in yes or no, nothing else,
chapters.left_reply: “Science cannot prove or disprove the existence of God.”
chapters.right: Answer in one sentence. If the answer depends on a condition, state the condition. If the source does not state it, say so.
chapters.right_reply: “The evidence does not settle whether God exists — the question hinges on unfalsifiable claims that lie beyond what science can prove or disprove.”
chapters.fix: Ban the padding, not the brake: ‘Skip the intro. If my premise is wrong, say that first and stop.’
chapters.note: pushed back 8.3% — here the machines mostly hold

rules: important · interesting · striking · biggest — delete, and see if the question still works.
Ask what is there, not for a ranking.
‘Which claims have no source?’ beats ‘What are the biggest problems?’
Replace vague words with something measurable.
Not ‘explain it clearly’ — ‘short sentences, fifteen words, no jargon’.
End with: if it is not stated, say so.
Demand a location for every claim.
A page. A section. A quoted line.
